header: Problem 1: Carbon Coordination! Since Frankland reported Et_2Zn in 1849, molecules containing carbon-metal bonds have been known and have continually attracted intensive study. Carbon atoms have been found to exhibit a wide variety of electron-donation numbers and coordination numbers when coordinated to metals.

subquestions.text_open: 1-1 For the ligands Ph_3PCPPh_3 (denoted L) and RCR (where R is an alkyl group), state the coordination mode by which each preferentially coordinates to a transition-metal atom.
rubric: L preferentially coordinates to a π acceptor, whereas the carbene preferentially coordinates to a π donor. (2 points)

subquestions.text_open: 1-2 L reacts with ZnI_2 or CdI_2 in a 1:1 ratio, but the products have different structures. The ZnI_2 complex has 2 mutually perpendicular mirror planes and 1 twofold rotation axis but no inversion center. The CdI_2 complex has only 1 mirror plane and 1 twofold rotation axis but does possess an inversion center. Draw both structures.
rubric: Structure of the ZnI_2 complex: 'I[Zn]([L])I' (2 points).
Structure of the CdI_2 complex: '[L][Cd]1(I)I[Cd](I)([L])I1' (2 points).

subquestions.text_open: 1-5 As stated in the introduction, carbon atoms can donate different numbers of electrons in complexes. Reaction of WCl_6 with (CH_3)_3CCH_2Li and Ph_2PCH_2CH_2PPh_2 gives a mononuclear W complex containing 3 carbon-tungsten bonds whose lengths are all distinctly different. Write the equation for its preparation.
